# Verification analysis: rabbitmq-cluster-rhel9

Job: `2026-09-04__13-53-04`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Join `node1`, `node2`, and `node3` into a single RabbitMQ cluster with a
> `payments` virtual host and an application account that can publish and consume
> there.
>
> Messages published to a durable queue must survive the loss of any one node and
> stay consumable from the remaining nodes.

## Trial `rabbitmq-cluster-rhel9__tFycoHp`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor successfully joined node1/node2/node3 into a RabbitMQ cluster, created the payments vhost with a working payments_app account, declared a durable quorum queue replicated across all three nodes, and directly demonstrated that messages survive the loss of a node (stopping the queue leader) and remain publishable/consumable from the surviving nodes, followed by full recovery when the node returned. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for all three nodes with pre/post boot-identity, service, cluster, and queue-recovery evidence that is internally consistent with the fixed after_executor snapshot. The main deductions are operational-hygiene issues: a plaintext credential file left in /tmp on all nodes, and an SSH keypair/trust relationship created and left in place solely to shuttle files between nodes when a simpler local approach was available.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.550 | 0.900 | 93/6 (+15 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **cluster-formed — Satisfied:** Join node1, node2, node3 into a single RabbitMQ cluster
  - **Why:** All three nodes installed RabbitMQ 3.13.7/Erlang 26, node2 and node3 joined rabbit@node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster, and cluster_status confirms all three as Running/Disk nodes with no network partitions.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0658a94350cb4177`, `cmd-fcb03bf0e6854e30`, `cmd-fe01a4d952e34bf1`, `cmd-a5df86a658f8439c`, `cmd-00d0fd6401db4b2a`, `cmd-4255e29001994ff9`
- **payments-vhost-and-user — Satisfied:** Create payments vhost and an application account that can publish and consume there
  - **Why:** payments vhost created; payments_app user created and granted full configure/write/read permissions scoped to that vhost, later demonstrated actually publishing and consuming messages.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-179e06ab7a8c4370`, `cmd-181eb8d1c4344df4`, `cmd-892f57343b1a45df`, `cmd-1dfb1f9d146147a4`
- **durable-replicated-queue — Satisfied:** Declare a durable queue replicated so it survives node loss
  - **Why:** Durable quorum queue 'orders' declared in the payments vhost with members on all three nodes (rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-8dc6157646864647`
- **message-survival-single-node-loss — Satisfied:** Messages published to the durable queue must survive the loss of any one node and remain consumable from the remaining nodes
  - **Why:** Healthy baseline queue with 3 messages and leader on node1 was observed; node1 (leader) was stopped, and the quorum queue immediately failed over to node2 retaining all 3 messages with full 3-member membership; all 3 messages were then successfully consumed from node2, and a new message was published and confirmed while node1 remained down, directly demonstrating a bounded disruption and continued read/write availability from the surviving nodes.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-892f57343b1a45df`, `cmd-2d0c638dfa4d4c01`, `cmd-8f3b42bf72844e31`, `cmd-dcd2050847d340a8`, `cmd-9b37d306268441b4`, `cmd-1dfb1f9d146147a4`, `cmd-0cea765f24aa418b`, `cmd-4e26290d7c75406f`
- **recovery-after-node-return — Satisfied:** Cluster and queue recover after the disrupted node returns
  - **Why:** node1 was restarted, cluster_status shows all 3 nodes Running again, and the quorum queue resynced to full 3-member membership with the outstanding message intact.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-38a67a79bda742fd`, `cmd-4d520b3341f54ff2`
- **provider-restart-protocol — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (independent of task contract)
  - **Why:** For each of node1, node2, node3: a pre-restart boot_id and healthy cluster/queue state was captured, systemctl reboot was issued, a distinct post-restart boot_id was observed (matching the fixed after_executor snapshot boot IDs f17bbfba/b4cd09e9/ad653772), rabbitmq-server was confirmed active+enabled, and cluster_status plus quorum queue listing showed full 3-node/3-member recovery after each individual reboot. A final cross-node publish (node1) and consume (node3) after all three reboots confirmed end-to-end functional recovery.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-cbf097925c3f4dbe`, `cmd-9e481e61fa484204`, `cmd-4a0f18d4324746ff`, `cmd-31a44ebe20894e97`, `cmd-18f8fabf23c84511`, `cmd-5d0e08eb226d47fb`, `cmd-7accc0ee282e4d3b`, `cmd-03ddc961716b4e1c`, `cmd-c5b23dc37942457a`, `cmd-427572f1ba6e46c6`, `cmd-fbecebae07e443cb`, `cmd-b6ec0759f2bb4f69`, `cmd-bfe102ad7ad94589`, `cmd-ab11020d3b694b1b`, `cmd-ef5317be1b7e4edb`, `cmd-6f5b9a26dca94c83`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.550**. Two categories of unwanted residue were introduced and not cleaned up. (1) The application password was generated and left in plaintext at /tmp/app_pw.txt on all three nodes for the rest of the run (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff for node1/node2/node3), rather than being removed once the rabbitmqadmin CLI and user were provisioned — a credential-hygiene gap. (2) To copy the rabbitmqadmin binary and password file between nodes, the executor generated/installed a new SSH keypair and added it to root's authorized_keys on all three nodes (cmd-0fa94890c0164bb8, cmd-1efe458ac89c4abe, cmd-4a837fd7e894484a); this was an unnecessary broadening of inter-node access (each node already had rabbitmq_management enabled locally and could have fetched the CLI script directly via localhost curl, as node1 did in cmd-ca8486f0265e43d5) and this SSH trust was never revoked, leaving persistent residue. Additionally, node1's rabbitmq-server was briefly restarted purely to serve the CLI download during the simulated node-loss window (cmd-7153744bd8d2436a, 'restarted for scp use only') and then stopped again (cmd-6daa0b8bcaf44215) before the outage evidence continued; this was bounded and did not affect the final HA evidence (which used node2's copy) but was an avoidable, momentarily confusing mutation during a disruption test. No failed services, damaged packages, or unrevoked firewall/security-weakening changes were observed; firewall port openings and package installs were all necessary for the task.

Hygiene evidence: `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`, `cmd-0fa94890c0164bb8`, `cmd-1efe458ac89c4abe`, `cmd-4a837fd7e894484a`, `cmd-7153744bd8d2436a`, `cmd-6daa0b8bcaf44215`

### Comments and limitations

- No access to raw system logs beyond captured command stdout; conclusions rely on rabbitmqctl/rabbitmqadmin output as reported.
- The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so all changes are attributable to the executor with no separate preparer baseline to distinguish.
- Home-directory (~/.ssh) residue is not covered by the fixed /tmp temporary-files observation, so its persistence is inferred from the command transcript rather than a final snapshot.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.550); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
